summary: Pointe-Ouest light, Anticosti: first lit 1858 in a stone tower; Malouin family keepers; 1950 fire; tower blasted in 1961 or 1967; steel tower automated 1979; keepers' houses now an inn.

lens.note: Second-order Fresnel lens of 1858. LighthouseFriends says fixed white; the register says rotating (unresolved).

light.note: Current light on a steel skeleton tower, year round (Coast Guard list entry 1523).

structures.note: Stone tower (register: walls of local limestone) with a refractory fire-brick lining inside (register) or two layers of white fire brick as outer covering (LighthouseFriends). 33 m (108 ft) per the register; LighthouseFriends gives 109.5 ft from base to vane. Demolished in 1961 (register: blasted down) or 1967 (LighthouseFriends, Route des phares).
Steel skeleton tower carrying the current light.
Two keepers' dwellings dating from the 1950s, now the Auberge de la Pointe-Ouest. The register lists remains of the old keeper's residence on the site.

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard lighthouse. Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Dirt road of about 16 km from Port-Menier, signposted to the Auberge.

stay.note: Auberge de la Pointe-Ouest in the two keepers' dwellings, operated by the Municipality of Anticosti Island; overnight stays (LighthouseFriends; Route des phares).

events.note: Province of Canada signs a contract with Charles-François-Xavier Baby for four lighthouses, including Anticosti's west point (LighthouseFriends)
Tower completed except for the lantern and lighting apparatus (LighthouseFriends); the Dictionary of Canadian Biography records Baby's 1856 Anticosti contract
Mechanics from France fit the lantern and lens and train the keepers (LighthouseFriends)
Light first shown 15 March 1858 (LighthouseFriends); the register dates it to 1858
House of refuge and provision depot built near the station (LighthouseFriends)
Exterior of the tower clapboarded, bricks having failed (LighthouseFriends)
Breakwater built to protect the tower from the sea (LighthouseFriends)
Bark Northumbria wrecked on Anticosti in November; crew supplied from the depot (LighthouseFriends)
Two vertical red stripes painted on the white tower (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper's residence catches fire in a severe storm; a defective chimney is blamed; little damage (Chief Engineer's report)
Cotton-powder fog signal at West Point fired every 15 minutes, not 20; 5-minute intervals when a ship's signal is heard near shore (Chief Engineer's report)
Fog signal building added to the station to house a diaphone plant (LighthouseFriends)
Fire damages the tower from an adjacent building (register); LighthouseFriends says it destroyed the living quarters attached to the tower
Government ship Chesterfield supplies the station; oil landed through the surf (LighthouseFriends quoting W. A. Calladine)
Old stone tower blasted down because the structure had become unstable (register). LighthouseFriends and the Route des phares date the demolition to 1967.
Steel skeleton tower replaces the stone tower (register; LighthouseFriends; Route des phares)
Trawler Calou, of Gaspé, runs aground near West Point in April (LighthouseFriends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Demolition of the stone tower: the register says it was blasted down in 1961 after the 1950 fire damaged it; LighthouseFriends and the Route des phares give 1967, the year the steel tower went up. Not resolved; the 1961 date comes from an official register, the 1967 date from two popular sources.
Lens: LighthouseFriends says the 1858 light was fixed white from a second-order Fresnel lens; the register describes a rotating second-order Fresnel lens. Not resolved.
Fire brick: LighthouseFriends says the tower had two layers of white fire brick as its outer covering; the register says the tower was lined inside with refractory brick. Not resolved.

1950 fire: the register says it damaged the tower from an adjacent building; LighthouseFriends says it destroyed the living quarters attached to the tower. These can both be true; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: 1) Checked on the page images and text. The 1908 keeper table (Appendix No. 12, scan p. 192) lists 'west point' against 'Alf. Malouin' on the same row, appointed 1 July 1877, salary $850; the keeper is matched by row on the image, not by OCR column order. 2) The 1900 Chief Engineer's report (scan p. 56, printed p. 41) gives the fire, the $10 allowance, 'Total expenditure, $165' under the West Point entry, the Menier survey and the one-acre purchase; the story cites p. 41 only. 3) The 1901 fog-signal change (scan p. 71, printed p. 56) sits under the Chief Engineer's 'changes and improvements in existing aids' with the heading 'Explosive signals increased in frequency'. 4) Demolition year of the stone tower: 1961 (register) vs 1967 (LighthouseFriends, Route des phares). Unresolved. 5) Lens: fixed white (LighthouseFriends) vs rotating (register). Unresolved. 6) Fire brick: outer covering (LighthouseFriends) vs inner lining (register). Unresolved. 7) The 1950 fire: the register says it damaged the tower from an adjacent building; LighthouseFriends says it destroyed the living quarters attached to the tower. Both date a fire to about 1950. 8) Horatio Malouin's dates (1928-1938) are as LighthouseFriends gives them; no second source read. 9) The 1907 letter and J. U. Gregory's evidence to the Royal Commission come only from LighthouseFriends; the Commission's record was not read. 10) The Northumbria wreck (1877) is placed only 'on Anticosti' by LighthouseFriends. 11) The 1953 supply-run passage is LighthouseFriends quoting W. A. Calladine's note in News on the D.O.T. (August 1953); that newsletter was not read. 12) LighthouseFriends and the Route des phares are read for facts; the story paraphrases LighthouseFriends' prose. Route des phares gives the directions from Port-Menier and the 1967 demolition; it does not mention overnight stays or the distance. 13) Living people: keepers Louis Henley, Luc Caron and Jean-Eudes Rioux served after 1960; they are named only as LighthouseFriends lists them, in their public role. 14) Record: stay type 'inn' is consistent with LighthouseFriends and the Route des phares; the record's visit fields are not contradicted. 15) No photos sourced.
